relevant_laws.quote: Upon all highways of sufficient width a vehicle must be driven upon the right half of the highway, except as follows: (a) When overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction under the laws governing such movements [NRS-484B-207-1, NRS-484B-210-1, NRS-484B-213-1, NRS-484B-213-2a, NRS-484B-213-2b, NRS-484B-213-2c]; (b) When the right half of the highway is closed to traffic; (c) Upon a highway divided into three lanes for traffic under the laws applicable thereon [NRS-484B-223-2]; (d) Upon a highway designated and posted for one-way traffic; or (e) When the highway is not of sufficient width.
relevant_laws.notes: A roadway obstruction might close the right half and affect where the driver may travel; two-way width and the obstruction’s location must be checked.

relevant_laws.quote: A vehicle must not be driven to the left side of the highway at any time: When approaching the crest of a grade or upon a curve in the highway where the driver’s view is obstructed within such distance as to create a hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction. Subsection 2 does not apply upon a one-way highway.
relevant_laws.notes: A winding road can contain a curve. This rule becomes live only if the driver goes left of center and the view is obstructed enough to create a hazard; the named obstruction need not be a sight obstruction.

relevant_laws.quote: Every vehicle driven upon a divided highway must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn, except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.
relevant_laws.notes: A winding road could also be divided, but no divided roadway or median is given. Review only if the turn crosses a divider.

relevant_laws.quote: it is unlawful for any driver to disobey the instructions of any official traffic-control device placed in accordance with the provisions of chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS
relevant_laws.notes: Would apply if an official device governs this location, such as a no-U-turn sign; none is stated. This is the general device-obedience rule behind NRS-484B-403-2.

relevant_laws.quote: The driver of a vehicle shall not make a U-turn in an area designated as a school zone or school crossing zone except:
relevant_laws.notes: Requires an active school zone or school-crossing zone, which the scenario does not specify. The U-turn is the direct match.

relevant_laws.quote: A U-turn may be made on any road where the turn can be made with safety
relevant_laws.notes: Direct U-turn safety rule; the obstruction and winding geometry can matter to whether the turn can be made safely. Its cited exceptions require separate facts.

relevant_laws.quote: If an official traffic-control device indicates that a U-turn is prohibited, the driver shall obey the directions of the device.
relevant_laws.notes: Requires a governing no-U-turn device, not given. LVMC-11-40-080 describes the same signed U-turn restriction for a cyclist/scooter subject.

relevant_laws.quote: The driver of a vehicle shall not make a U-turn in a business district, except at an intersection or on a divided highway where an appropriate opening or crossing place exists.
relevant_laws.notes: Requires a business district; a winding road could be in one, but district and intersection/divided-highway exceptions are unknown.

relevant_laws.quote: A vehicle shall not be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction upon any curve, or upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade, where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.
relevant_laws.notes: Directly concerns reversal on a curve. Check whether this winding-road segment is a curve and whether approaching drivers can see the vehicle within 500 feet.

relevant_laws.quote: A driver shall not turn a vehicle from a direct course upon a highway unless and until such movement can be made with reasonable safety, and then only after giving a clearly audible signal by sounding the horn if any pedestrian may be affected by such movement and after giving an appropriate signal if any other vehicle may be affected by such movement.
relevant_laws.notes: A U-turn changes direct course. The signal duties depend on whether a pedestrian or another vehicle may be affected. NRS-484B-768-1 addresses the analogous cyclist/scooter turning event.

relevant_laws.quote: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during not less than the last 100 feet traveled in a business or residential district and not less than the last 300 feet traveled in any other area prior to changing the course of a vehicle. This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.
relevant_laws.notes: The U-turn changes course; signal distance depends on business/residential district versus other area.

relevant_laws.quote: A driver shall not stop or suddenly decrease the speed of a vehicle without first giving an appropriate signal to the driver of any vehicle immediately to the rear.
relevant_laws.notes: Could arise if the driver stops or sharply slows for the obstruction or turn and another vehicle is immediately behind; neither fact is given.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at: A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.
relevant_laws.notes: Reasonable-speed duty applies while driving; a winding road and obstruction are relevant conditions. The extracted subject is driver; cyclist/scooter speed duties are separately listed.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at: Such a rate of speed as to endanger the life, limb or property of any person.
relevant_laws.notes: Broad prohibition on an endangering speed; no speed or endangerment outcome is assumed.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at: A rate of speed greater than that posted by a public authority for the particular portion of highway being traversed.
relevant_laws.notes: Would apply if a speed limit is posted for this segment; no sign or speed is specified.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character at: In any event, a rate of speed greater than 80 miles per hour.
relevant_laws.notes: Absolute speed cap applies on a highway; exceeding it is unlikely during a U-turn, but speed before the maneuver is unspecified.

relevant_laws.quote: The fact that the speed of a vehicle is lower than the prescribed limits does not relieve a driver from the duty to decrease speed when approaching and crossing an intersection, when approaching and going around a curve, when approaching a hill crest, when traveling upon any narrow or winding highway, or when special hazards exist or may exist with respect to pedestrians or other traffic, or by reason of weather or other highway conditions, and speed must be decreased as may be necessary to avoid colliding with any person, vehicle or other conveyance on or entering a highway in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care.
relevant_laws.notes: The law expressly names a winding highway and possible special hazards; it is a direct layout match, with speed reduction assessed only if necessary.

relevant_laws.quote: A person shall not drive a motor vehicle at such a slow speed as to impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic except when reduced speed is necessary for safe operation or in compliance with law.
relevant_laws.notes: Could matter if slowing for the obstruction impedes following traffic and reduced speed is not necessary for safety; no following traffic is stated.

relevant_laws.quote: A person shall not bring a vehicle to a complete stop upon a roadway so as to impede or block the normal and reasonable movement of traffic unless the stop is necessary for safe operation or in compliance with law.
relevant_laws.notes: Could matter if the driver comes to a full stop on the roadway and blocks traffic while negotiating the obstruction; a safety-necessary stop is excepted.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for a person to: Drive a vehicle in willful or wanton disregard of the safety of persons or property on a highway or premises to which the public has access.
relevant_laws.notes: Broad reckless-driving prohibition; the scenario does not itself establish willful or wanton disregard.

relevant_laws.quote: No vehicle in front of the driveway, entrance or approaches to a fire station shall be turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction.
relevant_laws.notes: A U-turn at a fire-station entrance would be covered, but neither a fire station nor Las Vegas location is stated.

relevant_laws.quote: The prima facie speed limit is twenty-five miles per hour on all streets and highways unless a different speed limit is posted as set forth in this Title [NRS-484B-600-1c].
relevant_laws.notes: Only if this road is within the City and no different speed limit is posted.

relevant_laws.quote: A person shall, when operating a vehicle, give his full time and attention to the operation of the vehicle.
relevant_laws.notes: General attention duty for vehicle operation; city-law applicability depends on the scenario location.

relevant_laws.quote: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate a vehicle of any kind or character in a careless or imprudent manner on any highway in the City.
relevant_laws.notes: General careful-operation duty on a City highway; the winding road and obstruction could affect prudent operation, but City location is unknown.

relevant_laws.quote: The operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter shall not: Intentionally interfere with the movement of a motor vehicle.
relevant_laws.notes: Could matter if the cyclist/scooter rider intentionally interferes with a motor vehicle while making the U-turn; no motor vehicle or intent is stated.

relevant_laws.quote: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 2, an operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter upon a roadway shall not turn from a direct course unless the movement may be made with reasonable safety and the operator gives an appropriate signal. The operator shall give the appropriate signal at least one time but is not required to give the signal continuously. An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter is not required to give a signal if: (a) The bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter is in a designated turn lane; or (b) Safe operation of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter requires the operator to keep both hands on the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
relevant_laws.notes: Direct rule for a bicycle, e-bike or scooter turning from a direct course; the obstruction affects the safety judgment. Signal exceptions depend on lane and safe-handling facts. Analogous driver turning event: NRS-484B-413-1.

relevant_laws.quote: An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter upon a roadway shall give all signals by hand and arm in the manner required by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420], except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.
relevant_laws.notes: If a hand/arm turn signal is required under NRS-484B-768-1, this law specifies how the rider gives it; the act of signaling is not stated.

relevant_laws.quote: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter upon a roadway shall, except: (a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed commensurate with the speed of any nearby traffic; (b) When preparing to turn left; or (c) When doing so would not be safe, ride as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable, exercising due care when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction. For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation: (a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway. (b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.
relevant_laws.notes: The law expressly treats fixed or moving objects and surface hazards as reasons riding near the right may be unsafe. Check whether the obstruction impedes access to the right; this is the rider-side analogue of a road-position issue.

relevant_laws.quote: Except as otherwise provided in an ordinance enacted pursuant to NRS 484A.469 [DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A], an electric scooter may be operated: On a roadway, bicycle lane, path or route at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour.
relevant_laws.notes: Applies to the electric-scooter subtype on a roadway; not to every cyclist in this actor variant. A local ordinance can alter the rule.

relevant_laws.quote: Any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter shall obey the instructions of official traffic-control signals, signs and other control devices applicable to vehicles, unless otherwise directed by a Police Officer.
relevant_laws.notes: Would apply if an official signal, sign or device governs this rider; none is stated. LVMC-11-40-080 specifically addresses a no-U-turn sign.

relevant_laws.quote: Whenever authorized signs are erected indicating that no right turn, left turn or U-turn is permitted, it shall be unlawful for any person operating a bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter to disobey the direction of any such sign, except where such person dismounts from the bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter to make any such turn, in which event such person shall then obey the regulations applicable to pedestrians.
relevant_laws.notes: Requires an authorized no-U-turn sign and operation in the City; neither is stated. It addresses the same signed turn restriction for riders that NRS-484B-403-2 addresses for drivers.

relevant_laws.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a bicycle at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions then existing.
relevant_laws.notes: General reasonable-speed duty for the bicycle subtype only, if in the City; winding geometry and obstruction affect conditions.

relevant_laws.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to perform stunts or wheelies, ride on handlebars, operate at unsafe speeds, or engage in any other reckless behavior while operating an electric bicycle or electric scooter on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path or route designated for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use.
relevant_laws.notes: General unsafe-speed/reckless-behavior restriction for electric-bicycle or scooter subtype in the City; not a claim that any stunt occurs.

borderline_excluded.reason: Mentions an obstruction, but the obligated subject is a pedestrian bypassing a sidewalk obstruction, not either candidate actor.
Mentions a highway obstruction, but regulates stopping, standing or parking alongside it; the scenario maneuver is a U-turn.
Requires a left turn within an intersection and an oncoming vehicle; neither is supplied by this winding-road U-turn record.
A winding road is not necessarily a defile, canyon or mountain highway; the required geography is not supplied.
Concerns a U-turn while exiting a multi-lane roundabout; this cell specifies a winding road, not a roundabout.
Requires a one-mile course with multiple specified offenses and an immediate hazard, not merely a U-turn near an obstruction.
